text: A carrot's orange isn't just colour. What does it turn into?
Part of the answer is in your eyes.
The orange is beta-carotene, and your body converts it into vitamin A.
Vitamin A, in turn, makes pigments in your eyes that help you see in low light.
_note: 'Vitamin A makes…' lost the 'A' on both ASR models; 3 phrasings tested, this one verbatim on base.en and small.en

text: A hundred grams of raw carrot gives more than ninety percent of a day's vitamin A.
And one medium-sized carrot, about sixty grams, covers more than half.
_note: 'One medium carrot' was heard as 'carat' by base.en; this phrasing verbatim on both models
